title: CMS educator fears he might lose his job after $12.5M in much-needed funds withheld - NewsBreak
text: CHARLOTTE, N.C. (QUEEN CITY NEWS) — Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools is revealing its plan to deal with the federal government withholding $12.5 million in promised grant money . CMS officials say not having the promised federal money won’t impact students this year, but next year is when some tough choices would have to be made. “I don’t even know if I’m going to have a job next year,” said Peri Alletto, who teaches special education at West Mecklenburg High School. He says the funding for the program he’s a part of comes from the federal government. After seven years with CMS, Alletto says he’s considered leaving for a job in South Carolina. “That’s our biggest concern. We don’t know where the money’s coming from,” Alletto said. Some of the gap for this upcoming school year will be covered with carryover money from last year, but there will be cuts in areas like teacher development, supplemental resources and personalized instruction. “We’ll be ready to receive our students and our families, and they will not feel the impact at the student experience level,” said Dr. Melissa Balknight, CMS’s deputy superintendent. District officials say they can only survive like this for one year. If the money doesn’t come through, $12.5 million will need to be slashed from the budget. “If we cut the $12.5 million, it will be deep, it will be painful, and every student could feel that impact,” said Kelly Kluttz, CMS’s chief financial officer. The Trump administration claims the money was being misused and put toward programs that helped undocumented immigrants. North Carolina’s Democratic Attorney General Jeff Jackson says he has yet to see any proof of that and is suing to have the money released. “We can continue to ask our public and our taxpayers to advocate for what they feel we need in public schools,” Kluttz said. CMS says this temporary budget solution means there are job vacancies that won’t get filled, but it does allow the district to keep all its current staff.
